newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse off to good start in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse off to good start in Q1.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group said it was off to a good start in all of its business units in the first quarter of 1997 despite difficult business conditions at home and tough competition abroad.

The group also expects restructuring measures taken last year to have a substantial impact on 1997 business and to make a positive contribution to profit developments, Credit Suisse chairman Rainer Gut said in the text of a speech prepared for the annual shareholders meeting.

"We will have to battle with a difficult business environment in Switzerland at least during the current year. Worldwide we face tough competition. Nonetheless we've managed a good start in all business units in the first quarter of 1997," Gut said.

Credit Suisse Group made similar comments early in May when it said revenues from commissions and trading activities were significantly higher than in the year-ago period while expenses and provisions developed in line with management expectations.
It provided no figures for its first-quarter performance.

Gut also said in his speech that the group's goals for the current year and for the future in general were to further expand the group's position as a leading Swiss bank, to reduce its cost structure by at least 500 million Swiss francs and to reduce the number of branches to around 240 by the end of 1998 from 360 at present.
Credit Suisse will also intensify efforts to better match credit margins to risk levels of individual credits, Gut added.
